action: Attend Maria Santos's emergency task force session this week and come prepared with two things the council does not already have: (1) a street-level report from Community Connection Night attendance over the past two weeks — specifically, what displaced workers from the Hawkins location closure and related layoffs are saying about their immediate needs, their gaps in accessing existing retraining programs, and their awareness of the financial resources Kevin O'Brien has been presenting at office hours; (2) a one-page concept brief for a Financial Triage Navigator function at the community center — a structured, in-person service where a trained volunteer or part-time staff member sits with a community member for 45 minutes and maps their current financial situation against the programs, products, and pathways that actually exist. This is not a food bank. It is not a loan office. It is a place where someone who has no idea what their options are can leave with a prioritized, specific list of next steps. I am not asking the council to fund it today. I am telling them it is coming so they can reference it publicly as a concrete institutional response when they are facing nine protests and a contracting employment base.
